limitations: This create-only request is an explicit closure over the discovery assignment; an empty reviewer_added_requests array means no reviewer-added candidates were found.
Ranking evidence and candidate material fingerprints are copied exactly from the bound discovery capsule and do not replace final source review.

reviewer_added_requests.discovery_reason: Api-contract-design defines consumer-visible resource, request, response, error, replay, and compatibility semantics and requires mixed-consumer evidence, while contract-testing owns executable provider-consumer compatibility across named versions and explicit non-proof boundaries. Full material is required to distinguish contract design from the independent executable proof needed to close its compatibility claims.

Consumer-impact-analysis inventories known and unknown consumers and selects deprecation, migration, rollout, rollback, and removal conditions, while cleanup-deletion-governance owns the deletion unit, exit evidence, cleanup ordering, recovery limits, and post-mutation absence proof. Full material is required to verify the handoff from consumer readiness to an authorized deletion decision.

Data-format-contract-usage defines dialect, semantic states, schema evolution, generated lineage, and old-reader/new-writer behavior, while contract-testing proves named producer-consumer combinations, retained payloads, semantic expectations, and proof freshness. Full material is required to prevent schema or parser evidence from being treated as complete executable compatibility proof.

Data-migration-design owns source-to-target transition, mixed-version sequencing, backfill, resumability, rollback limits, and completion evidence, while cleanup-deletion-governance owns removal of obsolete schema, compatibility paths, generated remnants, and recovery artifacts after exit conditions are met. Full material is required to define when migration completion permits irreversible cleanup.

Data-model-design owns authoritative persisted identity, relationships, lifecycle, and enforceable invariants, while business-invariant-analysis establishes business vocabulary, rule authority, allowed and forbidden transitions, bypasses, and validation from source evidence. Full candidate material is required to ensure a database shape does not invent business truth and that accepted business invariants correctly constrain the persisted model.

Integration-change-builder aligns producer-consumer contracts and implements cross-boundary timeout, retry, authority, recovery, and reconciliation behavior, while architecture-impact-reviewer owns placement, dependency direction, structural alternatives, and the independent architecture verdict. Full material is required when an integration boundary also changes module ownership or dependency direction.

Model-boundary-mapping owns translation, null and default semantics, generated-versus-handwritten authority, validation ownership, and leakage prevention, while sdk-library-contract-design owns the consumed public surface, generated-client lineage, compatibility classification, adoption, and packed consumer proof. Full material is required to separate representation mapping from the externally consumed SDK contract it must preserve.

Sdk-library-contract-design treats errors as public behavior affecting compatibility, generated clients, adoption, and consumer proof, while error-code-design owns stable error identity, classification, safe detail, retry and remediation meaning, boundary mapping, and unknown-code behavior. Full material is required to verify the SDK-to-error-contract handoff without duplicating error semantics in the library skill.

Sql-professional-usage requires explicit SQL-visible transaction boundaries, isolation assumptions, lock order, retry class, and visibility but routes transaction protocol to a specialist, while transaction-consistency owns transaction scope, isolation, conflicts, and proving tests. Full candidate material is required to protect the SQL-semantic versus cross-operation consistency boundary.
